howTitle.en: Utilization is the number shops get wrong
howTitle.zh: 利用率是最容易自欺的那个数

howP.en: Shops quote from m² and assume 90% utilization. It is usually 75–85%, because a 2440×3300 jumbo rarely divides evenly by the cut size and the strip left over is too narrow to sell. The gap between assumed and real utilization is where the margin quietly disappears — on a ¥85/m² glass it is roughly ¥8/m² of pure loss, times every sheet you ever cut.
howP.zh: 报价习惯按平米算，默认利用率 90%。实际大多 75–85%，因为 2440×3300 的原片很少能被裁片整除，剩下那条边根本卖不掉。假设值和真实值之间那段，就是利润悄悄溜走的地方——85 元/㎡ 的玻璃，差不多每平米蒸发 8 块，张张都蒸发。

q.en: Why is my real utilization lower than the diagram suggests?
q.zh: 为什么实际利用率比图上看着低？

a.en: Because the diagram shows the largest clean block. In production the sheet is cut in strips, and the last strip is usually unusable. This calculation already accounts for the cut gap but assumes you can use every leftover region — treat its utilization as an upper bound.
a.zh: 因为图上画的是最大的一块整齐区域。实际生产是分条切的，最后一条往往用不上。这个计算已经扣了切割缝，但默认每块余料都能用——所以它的利用率是上限。

q.zh: 旋转一下一定会更好吗？

a.en: Not always, and sometimes it looks better but is worse on the floor because the grain direction matters. Float glass has no grain, so rotation is safe here — but if the customer specified orientation, lock it.
a.zh: 不一定，有时候算出来更好，车间里反而更差，因为纹路方向有讲究。浮法玻璃没有纹路，转 90° 是安全的；但客户指定了方向就得锁死。

a.en: Not here — tempering is charged per m² with a minimum charge per piece, and it has to happen after edging, so it belongs on the next line of your quote. Add it manually; this page stops at glass plus edging.
a.zh: 这里不算——钢化按平米收且每块有最低收费，而且必须在磨边之后，属于报价单的下一行。自己加；本页算到玻璃加磨边为止。
